# Jubilees Chapter 5 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 5:1 — Angels' motivation: "beautiful to look upon" vs. "beautiful"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "they were beautiful to look upon" | Full Ge'ez phrase |
| LOGOS | "they were beautiful" | Condensed formal |
| PNEUMA | "how beautiful these women were" | Natural phrasing |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "they were beautiful." The shortened form is adequate and natural. EMET's full phrase is accurate but slightly redundant; PNEUMA shifts focus to the angels' perspective ("looked down, saw").

---

## 5:5 — "found grace" vs. "found favor"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "found grace before the eyes of the LORD" | "Grace" = charis/hen, Ge'ez equivalent |
| LOGOS | "found favor in the eyes of the LORD" | Standard Gen 6:8 rendering |
| PNEUMA | "found favor in the LORD's eyes" | Same as LOGOS, slightly compressed |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS "found favor." "Favor" is the established English rendering of Gen 6:8; "grace" (EMET) is theologically loaded in a different direction.

---

## 5:8 — Giants' self-destruction: "sent the sword" vs. "unleashed war"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he sent the sword amongst them that each should slay his neighbor" | Literal instrument metaphor |
| LOGOS | "He sent the sword among them so that each would slay his neighbor" | Same, slight modernization |
| PNEUMA | "he unleashed war among the giants" | Interprets "sword" as warfare broadly |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Sent the sword among them" is the Ge'ez idiom for divinely decreed warfare and should be preserved literally rather than generalized as "war."

---

## 5:11 — "new and righteous nature" — scope of renewal

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he made for all his works a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature for ever" | Full literal including "whole nature" |
| LOGOS | "for all his works he made a new and righteous nature, so that they should not sin in their whole nature forever" | Same content, slightly cleaner syntax |
| PNEUMA | "He then remade the nature of all his creatures — fresh and righteous — so that they would never again sin against their own design" | "Against their own design" is an interpretive paraphrase |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "In their whole nature" is important — Jubilees is asserting a comprehensive ontological renewal post-flood. PNEUMA's "against their own design" domesticates the concept.

---

## 5:26 — "Lubar" — transliteration vs. explanation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "on the top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat" | Preserves Ge'ez toponym |
| LOGOS | "on top of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "on the summit of Lubar, one of the mountains of Ararat" | "Summit" for added precision |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. All three agree on "Lubar"; minor variation is "top" vs. "summit." "Top" is idiomatic and sufficient.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
